title: Mechanical Behavior of Bamboo Pulp Reinforced Cement Based Mortar
content: Mortars and concretes exhibit low energy absorption before failure. To improve fracture toughness, metallic and nonmetallic fibers are incorporated into cementitious matrices. This work presents an experimental study conducted to determine the mechanical properties and fracture resistance of cement-based composites reinforced with bamboo pulp, aiming to explore their potential as building materials. The composites were manufactured using a modified Hatschek process, producing 8 mm thick plates composed solely of Portland cement and bamboo pulp at contents of 8% and 14% of the weight of dry cement. In addition to compression and impact tests, three-point bending was carried out using unnotched and notched specimens of different notch root radii. The compressive, flexural and impact strengths, as well as the J-integral fracture resistance are presented and discussed. According to the results, increasing bamboo pulp content decreased compressive strength, elastic modulus and flexural load-carrying capacity of the material. In contrast, impact energy increased with increasing bamboo pulp content.
